saml.description: When SAML client metadata descriptor URL is used, signing/encryption certificates are cached and may remain valid until cache refresh based on metadata or cache provider settings.
saml.source: Creating a SAML client -> Use metadata descriptor URL
saml.note: Old certificates being accepted before metadata cache expiry is expected caching behavior, not immediate trust-anchor substitution.

saml.description: Admin changes to SAML client or identity-provider trust settings take effect as authorized configuration changes.
saml.source: Admin CLI and client/identity provider configuration docs
saml.note: Do not flag successful authentication after an admin changed trust anchors or provider settings; only old-trust acceptance after intended replacement and cache expiry is suspicious.

saml.description: After trust material rotation via metadata descriptor URL or downloaded keys, old keys may remain accepted until cache refresh/expiry.
saml.source: SAML client settings - Use metadata descriptor URL
saml.note: Acceptance before cache expiry is standard caching behavior, not a trust-anchor substitution bug.

saml.description: If an administrator updates SAML IdP/client trust settings, acceptance under the new trust anchor is expected.
saml.note: Do not flag successful login after admin-authorized trust change as a vulnerability.

saml.description: TOTP codes may be reusable within the valid time interval depending on OTP policy; TOTP does not inherently remember used passwords unless reusable-code policy forbids reuse.
saml.note: A repeated TOTP within its validity window can be by design depending on policy and timing; do not confuse with bearer/session replay.

saml.description: Bearer access tokens can be reused across multiple API calls until expiry.
saml.note: Do not flag ordinary bearer token reuse as replay.

saml.description: User filtering by username/email in admin queries is substring-based rather than exact matching.
saml.note: Multiple hits from search do not imply identity collision; confirm with direct user ID lookup.

saml.description: When SAML step-up authentication is not fully configured, Keycloak continues and returns AuthnContextClassRef 'urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:ac:classes:unspecified' instead of erroring.
saml.note: This fallback is for backward compatibility and should not be flagged as missing enforcement unless step-up was explicitly enabled and mapped.

saml.description: When SAML step-up feature or mappings are not configured, Keycloak may continue authentication and return AuthnContextClassRef 'unspecified' instead of failing.
saml.note: This fallback is documented for backward compatibility and should not be flagged as a bypass unless step-up was explicitly configured.

saml.constraint: create_tenant returns 201 with no body. The realm name is the value sent in params/body (`realm`), not a response field. Do NOT rely on captures from the response body for subsequent events.

For SAML I1 signature-validation default tests, create_provider/enable_auth_method MUST create the SAML IdP with default config first. Documentation states client-side signature validation is optional (`Client Signature Required`) and metadata/cert retrieval is separately configurable. To test insecure defaults, do NOT pre-enable signature requirements or metadata-based key retrieval unless the specific test is about hardened configuration.

For SAML issuer-validation tests, if the broker/provider configuration does not explicitly bind the IdP entity ID, issuer comparison may be skipped. The fuzzer MUST run a control with explicit trusted IdP entity ID configured and an attack with `idp_entity_id` set to an untrusted issuer to distinguish missing configuration from a validation bypass.

For SAML replay tests (I2), Keycloak documentation explicitly supports emitting `OneTimeUse` only when the client setting `Include OneTimeUse Condition` is enabled. The fuzzer MUST enable this setting on the SAML client before running `saml_one_time_use_replay`; otherwise absence of replay rejection is inconclusive because the assertion may not contain `<OneTimeUse/>`.

For SAML expiry tests (I2), Keycloak SAML clients have `Assertion Lifespan`; if unset, realm Access Token Lifespan is used. The fuzzer MUST keep client assertion lifespan long enough for control logins and then send an explicitly expired assertion (`expired_assertion=true`) to test NotOnOrAfter enforcement. Without a valid control login first, rejection may reflect broken setup rather than expiry enforcement.

Keycloak documents metadata/certificate caching for SAML clients when `Use metadata descriptor URL` is enabled. Old signing certificates may remain accepted until metadata cache refresh based on descriptor `cacheDuration`, `validUntil`, or cache provider policy. Do NOT flag old-key acceptance immediately after admin key rotation as I1/I3 unless testing after cache expiry/refresh.

For I3 config-change sequences involving SAML trust anchors or client settings, admin-authorized changes are BY DESIGN. A valid coherence test must show the same request evaluated inconsistently without an intervening authorized config change; do not treat successful login under newly updated IdP/client config as a vulnerability.

User search by username/email (`verify_entity_details_by_name`) is not exact-match only. Documentation states filtering does not use exact matching and behaves like `*value*`. For I4 collision tests, do NOT treat multiple search hits as identity collapse by itself; always confirm with direct ID lookup (`verify_entity_details`).

SAML client `Valid Redirect URIs` allow wildcards only at the end of a URL pattern. For authorization-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST use exact ACS/processing URLs or end-of-path wildcards only; broader wildcard assumptions can create false positives by making intentionally broad redirect acceptance an admin configuration choice.

SAML step-up / MFA-related tests must account for authentication-session behavior. Authentication sessions expire after the realm Login timeout (30 minutes by default), and other browser tabs may restart auth automatically using existing SSO. For I3 or MFA-bypass sequences, use a fresh flow per test and do not interpret automatic restart/SSO reuse across tabs as bypass.

For `saml_mfa_bypass_via_binding_rule`, Keycloak can enforce MFA through browser/post-broker flows, and docs explicitly recommend adding session-limit and other authenticators to Post Broker Login Flow for IdP logins. The fuzzer MUST configure the relevant post-broker/first-broker flow when testing SAML-broker MFA enforcement; otherwise a missing MFA challenge may be due to flow configuration, not a broker bypass.

Numeric sentinel: password policy `Hashing iterations` uses `-1` as a sentinel meaning 'use algorithm default iterations' (argon2=5, pbkdf2-sha512=210000, pbkdf2-sha256=600000, pbkdf2=1300000). Never assume `-1` disables hashing work; it selects a nonzero default.
Numeric sentinel: password policy `Maximum Authentication Age` uses `0` to mean 'always re-authenticate before password update'. Never assume `0` means use default or disable the check.
Numeric sentinel: user session limits use `0` to disable the realm/client session-count check. Never assume `0` means literal zero sessions allowed.

Numeric sentinel: WebAuthn `Timeout` default is `0`, and documentation states behavior then depends on the authenticator implementation. Never assume `0` means immediate expiry; it delegates timeout behavior to the client/authenticator.
Numeric sentinel: OIDC/SAML client secret rotation uses `Rotated Secret Expiration=0` to mean the old secret is removed immediately during rotation. Never assume `0` means default grace period.

For SAML IdP signature-validation tests (I1), create_provider/enable_auth_method MUST explicitly set config.validateSignature=true and config.wantAssertionsSigned=true when testing secure configurations. The documentation states signature validation is controlled by these settings; omitting them creates a permissive/default-style setup and can make attacker-signed assertions succeed by configuration rather than vulnerability.

For the insecure-default SAML signature test pattern saml_cert_substitution, the fuzzer MUST create the SAML IdP with default/minimal config and MUST NOT set validateSignature=true or wantAssertionsSigned=true. The default saml_login already signs with an attacker cert; success under that setup indicates insecure configuration defaults, not bypass of an explicitly enabled check.

For SAML issuer-validation tests (I1 saml_issuer_mismatch), the broker-side SAML IdP configuration SHOULD include the expected IdP entity identifier/trust settings when available. If issuer-binding settings are left unset, acceptance of a mismatched Issuer may reflect skipped issuer comparison due to incomplete configuration rather than a proof-integrity flaw.

For SAML audience/conditions tests (I5 saml_no_audience_restriction, saml_no_conditions, saml_wrong_audience), the target SAML client/application MUST be configured with a stable Client ID / SP entity ID and ACS URLs before testing. Keycloak matches SAML requests and audience semantics against client configuration; missing or overly broad redirect/processing URLs can cause false positives or unrelated routing failures.

SAML assertion lifetime is controlled by the SAML client Advanced setting Assertion Lifespan. If not specified, Keycloak uses the realm Access Token Lifespan. Do not hardcode expected expiry windows in oracles; read the configured client value or account for realm fallback. This affects I2 expired-assertion tests and I5 no-conditions/audience tests.

Numeric sentinel: SAML client Assertion Lifespan has a documented sentinel behavior of 'not specified' meaning use the realm Access Token Lifespan, not literal zero. Never assume an omitted/empty value disables expiry checks; it selects realm default lifetime.

Numeric sentinel: Password policy Hashing iterations uses -1 to mean use the algorithm default iteration count, not literal negative one and not disable hashing cost. Defaults vary by algorithm (argon2=5, pbkdf2-sha512=210000, pbkdf2-sha256=600000, pbkdf2=1300000).
Numeric sentinel: Maximum Authentication Age password policy uses 0 to mean always re-authenticate before password update, not 'use default' and not 'disable re-auth'. This is strict mode.
Numeric sentinel: User session limit authenticator uses 0 for maximum sessions and maximum client sessions to DISABLE the check, not literal zero sessions. Do not interpret 0 as deny-all.

For I2 SAML replay tests, include a CONTROL login with a fresh assertion before the replay/expired variant. Without a successful control, a failed attack login may be caused by broken provider/client wiring rather than replay or expiry enforcement.

For I2 saml_one_time_use_replay, the SAML SP/client under test should have 'Include OneTimeUse Condition' enabled when generating Keycloak-issued assertions, but broker-consumption tests must inject <OneTimeUse/> directly in the forged assertion. Success on second use with identical Assertion/@ID and OneTimeUse present indicates missing replay enforcement.

For I2 saml_assertion_id_replay, reuse the exact same Assertion/@ID across two saml_login events. Keycloak documentation discusses authentication sessions and SAML conditions but does not document a user-configurable replay cache toggle here; therefore the oracle must compare first-success/second-failure on identical assertion IDs, not merely two similar assertions.

For I3 flow-coherence tests involving browser/SAML authentication, Keycloak creates authentication sessions that expire after the realm Login timeout (30 minutes by default). Multi-step SAML sequences must complete within the same authentication session; otherwise failures may be due to expired auth session rather than coherence bugs.

For I3 multi-tab or repeated browser-flow tests, Keycloak may automatically restart authentication in other tabs when one tab completes login because of the shared SSO session. Do not treat automatic restart/re-authentication across tabs as session confusion; use a single controlled flow instance for SAML coherence tests.

For I3 admin config-change sequences, new logins evaluated under updated SAML client or IdP configuration are BY DESIGN. A valid coherence test must show inconsistent handling of the same in-flight request/session, not that an admin changed client/provider settings between separate logins.

For I3 trust-anchor rotation tests using SAML metadata descriptor URL or downloaded certificates, Keycloak caches certificates. Old keys may remain accepted until metadata/cache refresh conditions are met. Do not flag acceptance of old signing keys before cache refresh/expiry as a trust-anchor violation.

For I4 identity-collision tests on brokered SAML logins, Keycloak can create or link local accounts based on brokered identity information. Tests such as saml_email_binding_collision and unverified_email_account_linking MUST control broker settings like trustEmail, allowCreate, and first/post broker login flows; otherwise account linking/creation behavior may reflect configured brokering policy rather than unintended principal collapse.

User search via /admin/realms/{realm}/users does NOT use exact matching by default; documentation states filters can match patterns like *testuser*. For I4 collision checks, do not use search results alone as identity oracle. Cross-check with direct user ID lookups.

For I4 case/unicode/name collision tests, Keycloak user lookup by search endpoint is fuzzy and may return multiple candidates. Use direct IDs from creation/login where possible, and treat search as discovery only.

For I5 authorization tests using client scopes and roles, effective permissions are the intersection of user roles and client/client-scope role-scope mappings. A missing role in the token may be due to scope mapping configuration, not denial by the broker. Configure both the role assignment and the client scope linkage before testing escalation or overgrant.

For I5 downscoping/token-exchange related tests, Keycloak documents a client-policy executor downscope-assertion-grant-enforcer that must be explicitly configured. Without that executor, requesting broader scopes during token exchange may be allowed by configuration. Do not interpret broader exchanged scopes as a bug unless the downscoping policy is enabled or the test specifically targets absence of that hardening control.

For I5 SAML step-up / RequestedAuthnContext tests, if the step-up-authentication-saml feature is not enabled, or no URI-to-LoA mapping exists, or the AuthnContextClassRef mapper is absent, Keycloak will by design continue and return AuthnContextClassRef=unspecified instead of erroring. Do not flag this fallback as an authorization-binding violation unless the feature and mappings were explicitly configured.

For I3/I5 tests involving Minimum ACR Value on SAML clients, configure both the client Advanced setting minimum ACR and the realm/client ACR-to-LoA mapping. Without the mapping, RequestedAuthnContext evaluation may fall back to unspecified behavior and invalidate the oracle.

create_tenant returns 201 with no body in Keycloak Admin API usage. The realm name is the value supplied in params, not a response field. Do NOT rely on captures from the response body for subsequent operations.
create_tenant returns 201 with no body. The realm name is the value you supplied in params; do NOT expect a response field capture for subsequent operations.
saml.source: Admin CLI examples for create realms and OpenAPI POST /admin/realms

saml.constraint: For SAML signature-validation tests (I1), the fuzzer MUST explicitly configure the SAML identity provider trust settings in provider config. The documentation states Keycloak can require signed client documents and validate signatures, but this is configuration-dependent; a default-created SAML IdP without explicit signature-validation settings may not exercise signature checks as intended.
saml.source: Creating a SAML client; Identity provider operations docs

saml.constraint: For saml_issuer_mismatch tests (I1), the fuzzer MUST configure the expected IdP entity identifier/trust anchor on the SAML provider. If issuer-binding settings are omitted, a successful login may reflect incomplete setup rather than an issuer-validation bypass.
saml.source: SAML client creation and identity broker docs

saml.constraint: For SAML replay tests (I2), include a CONTROL login with a valid assertion before replaying the same assertion ID or OneTimeUse assertion. Otherwise a failed second login cannot be distinguished from a broken SAML broker setup.
saml.source: Authentication sessions and SAML step-up/assertion examples

saml.constraint: Authentication sessions expire after 30 minutes by default, controlled by the realm Login timeout. Multi-step SAML flows are session-bound; the executor MUST complete SP-initiated flow and forged SAMLResponse submission within this window or the broker will reject due to expired authentication session.

When testing I3 config-change sequences against SAML clients or IdPs, NEW logins under updated admin configuration are by design. A valid coherence test must compare behavior of the same logical flow before and after config change, not treat admin-authorized reconfiguration itself as a vulnerability.
saml.source: Authentication flows, client settings, identity provider management docs

saml.constraint: If User Session Count Limiter is configured in browser, direct grant, reset credentials, or post broker login flows, value 0 means the check is disabled for both realm and client session limits. Do not treat 0 as literal zero allowed sessions.

For SAML broker tests that rely on post-broker enforcement such as MFA or session limits, the relevant authenticator MUST be added to the Post Broker Login flow and configured on the identity provider. Otherwise SAML logins may legitimately bypass checks that are only present in browser/password flows.
saml.source: User session limits documentation; conditional flows docs

saml.constraint: For saml_mfa_bypass_via_binding_rule tests (I3), first verify the victim user is challenged for MFA in the browser/password flow, then ensure equivalent enforcement is configured in the post-broker login flow for the SAML identity provider. Without post-broker flow binding, SAML login without MFA can be by design.
saml.source: Conditional flows, browser flow, user session limits post broker flow guidance

saml.constraint: Valid Redirect URIs on clients use exact case-sensitive matching, with wildcards allowed only at the end of a URL pattern. For SAML ACS and IDP-initiated endpoints that rely on redirect validation, the fuzzer MUST register exact URLs or safe suffix wildcards; do not assume glob semantics in the middle of the string.
saml.source: SAML client settings; OIDC basic settings redirect URI semantics

saml.constraint: IDP-initiated SSO is disabled when the client's IDP-Initiated SSO URL Name is empty. Tests using /realms/{realm}/protocol/saml/clients/{url-name} MUST configure this field first.

When using metadata descriptor URLs for SAML client keys, certificates are cached and refreshed according to descriptor cacheDuration/validUntil or cache provider policy. Acceptance of old keys before cache expiry is by design; only acceptance after cache refresh window should be treated as suspicious.
saml.source: SAML client Signature and Encryption settings

saml.constraint: Assertion Lifespan on SAML clients, if unset, falls back to the realm Access Token Lifespan rather than literal zero. Do not assume missing or zero-like absence means no expiry; use explicit expired assertions for I2 tests.

For step-up SAML tests using RequestedAuthnContext, if the step-up-authentication-saml feature is not enabled, or no URI-to-LoA mapping exists, or the AuthnContextClassRef mapper is absent, Keycloak will by design continue and emit the unspecified AuthnContextClassRef instead of returning an error. Do not flag this fallback as a bypass unless the feature and mappings were explicitly configured.

For client secret rotation related setup values, Rotated Secret Expiration must always be less than Secret Expiration. Rotation does not happen automatically; it occurs on client update or regenerate-secret actions. Do not expect passive time-based rotation without an update event.

Password policy Hashing iterations uses sentinel -1 to mean 'use algorithm default' rather than literal negative or disabled. Defaults are algorithm-specific (for example argon2=5, pbkdf2-sha512=210000, pbkdf2-sha256=600000, pbkdf2=1300000). Never assume -1 disables hashing-iteration checks.
Maximum Authentication Age password policy uses sentinel 0 to mean the user must always re-authenticate before password update, not 'use default'.
WebAuthn timeout uses sentinel 0 with implementation-dependent behavior rather than strict zero timeout. Do not use 0 in timing-sensitive tests expecting immediate failure.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Each test sequence MUST create its own realm using create_tenant with a unique name (e.g., valence-i1-test). Do NOT create IdPs in the master realm — use enable_auth_method in the new realm. This prevents alias conflicts (409) between concurrent sequences.
environment_defaults.idp_fields_warning: Do NOT include syncMode in enable_auth_method params — older Keycloak versions reject it as an unrecognized field. Also do NOT include caseSensitiveOriginalUsername at the top level — it belongs inside the config object.
